name: Gallio
overview: Gallio was a male proconsul of Achaia, a Roman administrative region, as recorded in Acts 18:12. Beyond his official title, Scripture provides no additional personal details or tribal affiliation. His role as proconsul places him as a significant Roman authority figure during the early Christian era.
namesAndTitles: The only name recorded for this individual is 'Gallio,' a proper name mentioned in Acts 18:12. No specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to this name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Gallio beyond his role as proconsul of Achaia. There is no mention of relatives or other personal connections in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Gallio's importance in the biblical narrative stems from his position as proconsul, which situates him as a Roman official who interacted with the early Christian movement. His mention in Acts 18:12 provides historical anchoring for the events surrounding the Apostle Paul's ministry in Achaia. As a Roman authority, Gallio's role indirectly reflects the broader context of Christian witness under Roman governance.
